title: Cipher and Alibi
premise: When estate lawyer Isandro Blackwood is summoned to read the will of Marguerite Voss—a woman who vanished twenty years ago and was declared dead without a body—he discovers a will dated three years after her disappearance, and her diary, which continues writing entries long past the date she was last seen. Following the diary's coded references to a shipping ledger hidden in the town archive he himself curates, Isandro uncovers that Marguerite faked her death to expose a smuggling ring run by the founding families who had corrupted his own late mentor. As the tide begins yielding bones from the drowned cove, Isandro must choose between protecting the town's carefully filed lies and publishing the truth, ending with him decoding the final ledger entry: Marguerite's confession that she killed the man who threatened her daughter, then surrendered herself to the sea—and a living witness arriving at his office with the last page of the diary.
about_author: Tamsin Quintana spent a decade as a probate clerk in a coastal town before turning to fiction, a career that taught her that every family's fortune has a filing error somewhere. She writes mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the people who keep both in order.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro Blackwood, POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for Marguerite Voss, dated 2007—three years after her disappearance. Isandro, who probated her death himself, recognizes his dead mentor's notary stamp on the document. The emotional beat is dread wrapped in professional calm; his ordered world develops its first crack.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He searches his immaculate archive for Marguerite's file and finds it hollowed out—every page replaced with blank ledger paper except one diary page dated after her disappearance. Flashbacks establish twenty years of keeping the town's secrets. The beat: the archivist realizes the archive has been edited around him.

chapters.title: Reading of the Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with the Voss family present. He reads the impossible will aloud: everything left to 'the one who keeps the files,' contingent on recovering 'the tide's account.' Marguerite's brother Rowan threatens litigation; her estranged daughter Sable watches Isandro too closely. Beat: public pressure meets private compulsion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable Voss's POV, first appearance. Sable returns to town officially to contest the will, privately to learn why her mother vanished the week after their last fight. She interviews Isandro under the guise of discovery requests. Beat: two investigators circling each other, each hiding an inheritance of guilt.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Deciphering the diary's marginal numbers, he realizes they index the town's public shipping ledgers—volumes he has dusted for decades. The entries record cargo that never existed, payments routed through the founding families' cannery. Beat: revelation that the crime was always visible, curated by him.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, deep flashback chapter. How young Isandro helped his mentor Halbrook bury evidence of the smuggling ring in exchange for partnership, believing silence was mercy. The night Marguerite confronted Halbrook. Beat: the corruption of good intentions; power as a slow seduction.

chapters.title: Rowan's Version
chapters.summary: Rowan Voss's POV. Rowan recalls his sister as paranoid and reckless, insists she ran off with smugglers' money. But his narration betrays knowledge of the ledger's existence. He burns a box of Marguerite's letters that night. Beat: unreliable grief curdling into menace.

chapters.title: Diary, Continued
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. More diary pages surface, mailed anonymously, entries growing more frightened through 2007—Marguerite alive, hiding, watching someone. The handwriting matches the will's signature exactly. Beat: hope and horror entwined; the missing woman may have been murdered years later than anyone thought.

chapters.title: The Cannery's Quiet Partners
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable traces the founding families' descendants and finds them all still comfortable, still intermarried, still funding the town's memorial to her mother's 'tragic drowning.' One matriarch, Odile Crane, warns her gently to stop asking. Beat: power's inheritance passed down like china.

chapters.title: Halbrook's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In his mentor's old strongbox, Isandro finds Halbrook's own coded notes mirroring the ledger—and a note reading 'She gave me until the equinox.' Halbrook died the week after Marguerite disappeared. Beat: Isandro confronts the possibility his beloved mentor was murdered, or worse, a murderer.

chapters.title: Low Tide, First Bones
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A winter storm strips the cove; a hiker finds a human radius bone wearing a distinctive ring. Police reopen the case. Sable recognizes the ring from a childhood photograph. Beat: the sea begins testifying; grief becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Detective Amara Okafor, new to town and unburdened by its history, questions Isandro about the will's provenance. Their cat-and-mouse becomes an uneasy alliance when he shows her one decoded ledger page. Beat: the keeper of secrets testing whether truth-telling is survivable.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Watched
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reveals to Isandro that she received diary pages too—for years, postmarked locally. Her mother was alive in 2010, watching over her from inside town. The betrayal of silence cuts both ways. Beat: fury and longing fused; the theme of inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Odile's Tea
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Odile Crane invites Isandro for tea and offers him partnership, protection, a seat among the families—if the ledger stays decoded no further. She speaks of Marguerite with intimate hatred. Beat: explicit temptation; power offering him the same bargain his mentor took.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro/Sable POV. On the equinox anniversary, someone ransacks the archive, taking the ledger volumes but leaving the diary pages arranged like an accusation. Isandro realizes only three people knew the indexing code. Beat: paranoia peaks; the hunter is inside the walls.

chapters.title: The Third Set of Handwriting
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Forensics on the diary shows a third hand: some entries were continued by someone else after Marguerite stopped writing—an heir, keeping the record alive. Okafor suspects Sable; Isandro defends her. Beat: trust fracture between allies; mystery deepens rather than narrows.

chapters.title: Rowan Drowns His Secrets
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Confronting Rowan at his boathouse, Sable finds the stolen ledgers and Marguerite's original letters. Rowan confesses he helped his sister fake her death, then blackmailed the families for years using her ledger—until she tried to end it. They struggle; Rowan falls into dark water. Beat: accidental violence; the past repeating.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Wrote Last
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The final genuine diary entry, recovered from Rowan's safe: Marguerite caught Odile's son sabotaging her exposure plan; in the struggle he died. The families covered it up; Marguerite chose exile over prison, then chose the sea over exile. Beat: tragic clarity—the mystery resolves into moral ruin all around.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Divers recover remains in the cove: two bodies, twenty years apart—Halbrook and Marguerite's companion, plus evidence placing Odile's son there in 2004. Arrests ripple through the founding families. Odile, cornered, offers Isandro everything one last time. Beat: climax of institutional collapse.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro refuses Odile, publishes the full decoded ledger, and executes the will as written—naming himself trustee of the truth, not the money, which goes to the town. He resigns from the families' law practice. Beat: renunciation; the invisible man steps into daylight at real cost.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Isandro and Sable, alternating. At his office door stands an elderly lighthouse keeper's widow holding the diary's true final page: Marguerite didn't drown—she lived her last year in the keeper's cottage, dying naturally, leaving instructions that the truth surface only when the sea finished its testimony. Beat: grace note; mercy discovered inside the machinery of justice.

chapters.title: Cipher and Alibi
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. Spring: the archive reopens with the Voss papers displayed openly, nothing alphabetized into oblivion. Sable stays to rebuild; Isandro begins writing the town's honest history. Final image—he files the last document, then leaves the drawer open. Beat: resolution; memory inherited as obligation, not burden.
